newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end at year's high, still wary.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end at year's high, still wary.

text.p: Fuelled by a rally on Wall Street, Argentine stocks pushed to a new five-year high Thursday but were seen hesitant near-term, dealers said.

"The market was favored by the bullish international scenario today, but it may not be able to stand on its own two feet," said Humberto Lopez at traders Wainbuch. "The tone is very selective and caution prevails at these price levels."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV tacked on 0.9 percent to set a new five-year record of 831.44, piercing technical resistance at 830.
"There is a feeling the market is not ready for a sharp upswing. Instead it will probably seesaw higher while it consolidates recent gains," another dealer said.
Traders predicted business would be very slow Friday during the U.S. Independence Day holiday.
"I'm not even showing up," one fund manager said.
Floor volume picked up to 33.6 million pesos from 29.2 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 113.1 from 66.2 million Wednesday.
The broad market closed up 1.1 percent, with winners pounding losers 54 to 14 and 18 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier gainers were construction stocks Polledo and Juan Minetti, up 3.6 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively, and electricity generator Central Puerto, up 3.6 percent.

The only MerVal losers were carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, which shed 2.5 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively, real estate developer Irsa, which fell 1.3 percent, and holding company Garovaglio, off 1.1 percent.
